Riveting

RIV-it-ing -- three syllables, stress on the first syllable, RIV. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Riveting is completely engrossing.

The documentary about deep-sea volcanoes was so riveting that nobody touched the popcorn.

Worked Example

The librarian opens the book and reads only the first chapter aloud. When the recess bell rings, not one student moves -- twenty-six pairs of eyes stay locked on her, waiting for the next sentence.

That chapter was riveting: so completely engrossing that attention could not be pried away. The word comes from rivets, the metal pins that permanently fasten steel plates -- a riveting story fastens your attention just as firmly.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

gripping: Gripping holds your attention tightly, and it almost always squeezes with suspense -- a gripping thriller keeps you tense about what happens next. Riveting can fasten you to anything at all, tense or calm: a lecture, a chess match, even a budget meeting.

engrossing: Engrossing means absorbing all of your attention -- an engrossing puzzle swallows a whole afternoon before you notice. Riveting is that same total capture with force added: it does not just absorb you, it bolts you in place, unable to look away.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

dull: not interesting at all

monotonous: tiresomely unchanging

Where it sits · how firmly it holds your attention — captivating → riveting → mesmerizing

captivating vs. riveting: Captivating charms you -- a captivating melody makes you want to stay -- while riveting goes further: it pins you in place, unable to look away.

mesmerizing vs. riveting: Mesmerizing goes past even riveting: a riveting account keeps you alert, pinned to every word, while a mesmerizing one pulls you half into a trance -- you drift with it and lose track of the room.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — rivet

root — rivet: a metal pin that fastens; to fasten firmly (Old French river 'to fix, to fasten')

suffix — -ing

suffix — -ing: forming an adjective from a verb (Old English)

Put it together

Put it together: Riveting comes from rivet, the metal pin hammered flat to fasten plates of steel so they can never slip apart. Something riveting fastens your attention the same way -- eyes bolted in place, unable to wander.

Use the root in a new word: rivet

Use the root in a new word: rivet: Thousands of steel rivets hold the old bridge's plates together.

Root Check

Word Choice

Riveting praises anything that seizes total attention: a riveting account, testimony, or final set. It is stronger than interesting by a mile -- the image is mechanical, your eyes bolted to the thing -- so save it for moments when attention genuinely cannot wander.
